<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3ee6af44fd6b91b339358fb6f805584b1d2a1aac` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `136d3152c6db22bc6fe28fe0de637103f44d1316` — the merge of head `fec1ac66a9d50fd325b72aa2b97212ac12685d09` into base `3ee6af44fd6b91b339358fb6f805584b1d2a1aac`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 136d3152c6db22bc6fe28fe0de637103f44d1316 && git checkout 136d3152c6db22bc6fe28fe0de637103f44d1316
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3ee6af44fd6b91b339358fb6f805584b1d2a1aac fec1ac66a9d50fd325b72aa2b97212ac12685d09 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3ee6af44fd6b91b339358fb6f805584b1d2a1aac && git merge --no-ff fec1ac66a9d50fd325b72aa2b97212ac12685d09

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3ee6af44fd6b91b339358fb6f805584b1d2a1aac
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `238ee238bd1d77d7579623cec1bf417103b753eb`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/lint/src/validate-visibility-predicates.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.app-nav-visible-predicate-writes.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.draft-publish-verdict.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.runtime-authoring-gate.test.ts + packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts, packages/formula/src/registry.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/expression.zod.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-visibility-predicates.test.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.test.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts, ui/packages/core/src/evaluator/ExpressionEvaluator.ts, ui/packages/core/src/evaluator/fieldRules.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/providers/ExpressionProvider.tsx, examples/app-crm/src/apps/crm.app.ts. Not reviewed (prose face): .changeset/28726-nav-visible-over-budget.md, read for ② only.

Check-runs on the head at review time: 40 runs, 0 failed, 0 cancelled, 8 skipped, 11 completed green, 21 still in progress. Green: Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check PR Size, Flag docs affected by code changes, Plan Test Core shards, filter, Auto Label. Pending: Test Core 1-8, Build Core, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, the four Type Check jobs, the six Lint jobs. The pending families are the queue guard's to wait on; nothing here re-runs or pre-judges them.

### ① Derived judgments

1. App writes: a nav `visible` (top-level `navigation[]`, `areas[].navigation[]`, every `children[]`), as a bare string or a `{ dialect: 'cel', source }` envelope, that is valid CEL but overruns a `DEFAULT_LIMITS` bound is now refused with `visibility-predicate-over-budget` at the key path, severity error. RIGHT. The verdict is the one front end's (`celRefusal` already answered `kind: 'bounds'` from `parseCelToAstWithReason`; the walker only dropped it), the limits are formula's `DEFAULT_LIMITS` (`maxAstNodes` 256, `maxDepth` 32, `maxListElements` 64), and the console's CEL route (`ExpressionEvaluator#evaluateCelCondition` through formula's `ExpressionEngine`, whose environment is built with `CEL_ENV_OPTIONS.limits = DEFAULT_LIMITS`) refuses the same source at parse, after which `evaluateNavigationVisibility` withholds the entry. The dev measured exactly that in Chromium before the change. The spec declares the slot as CEL the engine must be able to run (app.zod.ts line 371, `EvaluatedExpressionInputSchema`); a predicate the engine cannot parse never worked for any viewer, so the refusal is the spec's own made real, not a capability withdrawn.
2. App writes: a chain inside the budget (51 clauses of the test's shape; 52 overruns) stays admitted; booleans, envelopes of another dialect and envelopes without a string `source` stay unjudged. RIGHT, unchanged from #28663, and pinned by the controls at both doors.
3. The bound named in the verdict is read off the front end's structured overrun through the shared `boundName`, so a `maxDepth` or `maxListElements` overrun on a nav entry names its own axis. RIGHT; no hard-coded bound.
4. No new rule id, export, limit or parser; `checkElement` untouched, so page and view wording stays byte-identical (the new test pins the page twin's `always renders` and `record.f in` remedy). RIGHT. Public surface of `@objectstack/lint` moves only in `os explain` prose: the nav paragraph on `visibility-predicate-over-budget`, and the syntax entry's sentence "Only the syntax is judged on a navigation entry", which this change makes false, now reads "only whether it parses is judged". Both meet the registry's pins (`covers` unchanged; no issue number in a paragraph).
5. One implementation at every surface: the save door, draft `_diagnostics` and publish read `judgeRuntimeAuthoringRules` over `AUTHORING_RULES` filtered by `runtimeTypes` (the family declares `app` since #28663), and the CLI reads `runAuthoringRules('validate')`; the protocol tests pin the draft read (`navigation.0.children.0.visible`), the 422 and the active save with the build's finding key by key. No `metadata-protocol` source edit. RIGHT.
6. The verdict sentence for one id is now built in two places (the element arm and `navOverBudgetFinding`), sharing `boundName` and `NAV_SURFACE`. Noted by the dev as a fold to make once #28725 (same file) lands; see ④ S2.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/28726-nav-visible-over-budget.md`: `@objectstack/lint` **minor**, BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, `Skills-docs: none` with its reason, one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with the no-conversion argument and the corpus count (1 nav `visible` in `examples/app-crm`, under budget, 0 refused). Matches what the diff publishes: a value shape an author could write is now refused at every door (narrowed), on the one package the diff moves; `metadata-protocol` changes are tests only, which publish nothing. The `(narrowing)` arm is the BREAKING one by AGENTS.md, and the kind takes at least minor. The PR body carries the same lines; Check Changeset and the PR-body guards are green on the head. The changeset's sentence superseding the #28663 changeset's "only the syntax is judged" line is right and does not edit the pending #28663 changeset. Clause-②: `no (narrowing)` is right; the claim comment's bare `no` is the seat's own line (③ item 1).

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none declared.

Deviations, each answered:
1. Claim line `Clause-②: no` versus PR body and changeset `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. Answered: the PR body and changeset are the records the gates read and they are right (`check-changeset-no-major` refuses `narrowed` beside a line without the arm). The seat amends its claim comment; no PR change.
2. One sentence of the syntax entry's nav paragraph edited beyond the order's "over-budget nav paragraph". Answered: the sentence became false with this change; leaving it would ship a lie in `os explain`. Inside the claimed file (`rule-explanations.ts`) and right.
3. Protocol test rows added in two `metadata-protocol` test files with no source edit. Answered: #28663's precedent, and the only way to prove the three doors; the claim's file surface names "their tests".

Out-of-scope findings, escalated rather than fixed here:
4. Two builders of the over-budget verdict sentence in one file. See ④ S2; the fold waits on #28725 in the same file.
5. `origin/main` moved after the gate loop (seven commits, none in this PR's files; merge-tree clean). Answered: CI on the head is the gate record; the pending families above are running on this exact head.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, read against the published spec on `main` and the consumer: the spec says a nav `visible` is CEL the engine runs; the console parses it under the same `DEFAULT_LIMITS` the lint parses under and withholds the entry on a parse fault; so an over-budget predicate never gated anything for any viewer, and refusing it at the author closes the same silent-disappearance route #28663 closed for syntax, with the id the page surface already carries. Attempts to break it: a 51-clause chain is admitted at every door (the front end's own boundary, not a lint guess); the three `DEFAULT_LIMITS` axes each name themselves through `boundName`; an envelope of another dialect is still the console's legacy path and is not judged; a syntax fault keeps its own id (the new test pins the syntax id silent on a size fault and vice versa); the page twin's wording is pinned unchanged; the differential at the door stays clean because `apps` is not a context collection. The remedy's two shapes (`current_user.positions.exists(p, p in [...])`, one `current_user.can(...)`) parse in the front end (`exists` is a CEL macro the spec's own `CEL_BINDING_MACROS` lists) and the dev evaluated both in the console; a list over `maxListElements` 64 inside the `exists` would be refused by the same id naming that axis, which the explanation's existing paragraph already says.

Findings:
- S1 (should-fix): the nav over-budget `hint` is 218 characters. `validate-visibility-predicates.test.ts` records the #22161 contract for this id's family, `visibility-predicate-over-budget` included: every firing variant is one remedy line of at most 200 characters. The pin walks only what that file fires (the element arm), so the suite stays green while the nav variant exceeds the id's recorded budget by 18 characters; the element hint is 179. Trim the example (drop the `such as` clause or shorten the list literal) under 200, and add the length pin to the #28726 block so the nav variant is held to the same line. Not a wrong verdict and not a capability taken away, so not a must-fix.
- S2 (should-fix, follow-up): the verdict sentence of one id is built twice (`checkElement`'s bounds arm and `navOverBudgetFinding`); fold them into one builder taking a `SyntaxSurface`-style surface, as `syntaxFinding` already does, once #28725 has landed in the same file.
- Must-fix: none.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-nqjz3m`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5oc56xChD6Wrc4cGSt`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fec1ac66a9d50fd325b72aa2b97212ac12685d09`
Local-runs: none
Scope: delta of the record in comment 6561551921 (head 238ee238bd1d77d7579623cec1bf417103b753eb, PASS with S1 and S2 should-fix): the one commit fec1ac66a, read as `git diff 238ee238 fec1ac66`, over packages/lint/src/validate-visibility-predicates.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.app-nav-visible-predicate-writes.test.ts + packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts (read at the head, for the alternative the hint now defers to) and packages/lint/src/validate-visibility-predicates.test.ts (the #22161 contract the pin mirrors). Not reviewed (prose face): .changeset/28726-nav-visible-over-budget.md, whose one-line edit is read for ② only. Everything the earlier record judged stands unchanged: the net diff against `main` at this head is the same six files (233 insertions, 10 deletions; three commits over `main`), and no other hunk moved.

Check-runs on the head: 63 runs, 54 success, 9 skipped, 0 failed, 0 cancelled, 0 pending (read with `--paginate`). Every family that was still in progress on the earlier head is green here: Test Core 1-8, Build Core, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, the Type Check jobs and the Lint jobs included.

### ① Derived judgments

1. The nav over-budget `hint` is now one example: "Make the predicate smaller: collapse an `||` chain into one list test, e.g. `current_user.positions.exists(p, p in ['a', 'b', …])`", 130 characters on the tree (was 218). The verdict `message` is unchanged at 171 characters with a named bound (the unnamed-bound form carries the front end's summary after the same 171-character prefix). RIGHT: inside the #22161 one-line budget of 200 the family records, and the dropped alternative (gate the entry on one `current_user.can('OBJECT', 'read')` check) is still in `os explain visibility-predicate-over-budget` at this head (rule-explanations.ts, the nav paragraph), which the builder's new comment points to. No accept-set change: the same predicates are refused and admitted as on the earlier head.
2. The new pin in the #28726 test block walks the nav variant: for each of the three `SITES` (top-level, inside an area, inside a group's children) it takes the over-budget finding the app door gives for the 90-clause chain and holds both `message` and `hint` to no newline and at most 200 characters. RIGHT and non-vacuous: it reads the real door (`gateApp`), the real id filter (`overBudget`), and would have failed on the earlier head's 218-character hint.
3. Nothing else moved: the delta is the hint string, its comment, the pin, and one changeset sentence. `checkElement`, the element wording, the walker's branch, the explanation entries and the protocol tests are byte-identical to the earlier head. RIGHT.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged: `@objectstack/lint` **minor**, BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, `Skills-docs: none`, the ADR-0087 marker. The one-line changeset edit restates the remedy as the hint now reads (one example, with the `current_user.can(…)` alternative named as the `os explain` entry's). Still what the diff publishes; Check Changeset is green on this head. Clause-②: `no (narrowing)` is right.

### ③ Boundary flags

No new dev flags and no `open_questions` on this delta. The earlier record's items stand: the claim comment's bare `Clause-②: no` is the seat's own line to amend; S2 (fold the two builders of the over-budget sentence once #28725 lands in the same file) stays a follow-up, untouched by this commit as expected.

### ④ Design judgment

S1 of comment 6561551921 is closed on the tree: the nav variant of `visibility-predicate-over-budget` now meets the id's recorded one-line budget, the pin holds every nav site to it so the budget cannot drift again on this surface, and the remedy loses nothing an author needs (the second shape is one `os explain` away, as the element arm's own remedy already works). Attempts to break it: the pin covers the three sites and both lines; the hint's one example is the collapse the front end accepts (`exists` is a CEL macro; a list inside it is bounded by `maxListElements` 64, which the explanation says); the message length cannot grow past the budget on another axis (`maxDepth`, `maxListElements` name themselves through `boundName` within the same prefix). The narrowing judged on the earlier head is unchanged and still the spec's own refusal made real.

Findings:
- Must-fix: none.
- Should-fix: none new. S2 (two builders of one sentence) remains the follow-up the earlier record named.

**ACCEPT** · `domain:server` seat 5 · `os-project-manager` · `session_01FEkQ5oc56xChD6Wrc4cGSt` · 2026-11-01T18:18Z · head `fec1ac66` · #28726

The maintainer's standing authorisation for landing reviewed PRs, verbatim: 「按照 pm-dispatch 规则复核过的都授权」.

席位意见:与 diff 相符。导航 `visible` 写得过大(语法对但超出 CEL 解析预算)时，以前保存成功、控制台却对所有人隐藏该入口；现在保存、草稿诊断、发布和 `os validate` 都会拒绝并给出缩写建议。开发先在浏览器里实测确认了控制台确实隐藏。

1. **Shape:** draft against `main`, `Fixes #28726`, `@objectstack/lint` **minor** changeset with the BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, `Skills-docs: none` with its reason, ADR-0087 marker. `check-governed-merges --pr 28756`: NOT governed, +233 / -10. `git merge-tree` against `main`: clean. Landing tier S.
2. **Against the order:** ruling 1 measured first in Chromium on a stock showcase boot (base: the 90-clause entry withheld, `[bounds] Exceeded maxAstNodes (256)`; its one-clause twin rendered). Ruling 2: the nav walker keeps both arms of `celRefusal`, the bounds arm as the existing `visibility-predicate-over-budget` with the nav consequence; no new id, parser or limit; `checkElement` untouched.
3. **Accepted deviations:** one sentence of the `visibility-predicate-syntax` explanation's nav paragraph ("only the syntax is judged") restated, since this change made it false. Rework on this head: the nav hint cut to one example (130 characters) with a #22161 length pin over all three nav sites (red at 218); the PR body's finding bullet updated by the seat through the relay. The claim's `Clause-②: no` is the claim template's line; the PR body and changeset carry the `(narrowing)` arm the gates read.
4. **Gates:** `## Contract review` at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`: **PASS** on `238ee238` (comment 6561551921) and delta **PASS** on this head (comment 6561941305), no must-fix. Check-runs on this head: 54 success, 9 skipped, 0 failed. Dev: 59/59 derived families, `--ran` 0 NOT-MEASURED.
5. **Out of scope:** review S2 (the over-budget verdict sentence is built in two places, `checkElement` and `navOverBudgetFinding`) waits for #28725, which edits the same file. It rides #28725's order as a fold, so no separate card ⇒ Acceptance notes.
6. **Landing:** `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` through the relay.
